text.p: HFS Inc said it has reorganized its senior management structure, creating an office of the chairman to direct the company's operations.

The office of the chairman includes Stephen P. Holmes, formerly executive vice president and chief financial officer, who has become vice chairman and to whom certain of the company's business units will report.
The office also will include John D. Snodgrass, president and chief operating officer, who has the added title of vice chairman.
He will be responsible for the company's hotel and real estate businesses as well as the company's expanding preferred vendor activities.
HFS also said that Michael P. Monaco has become vice chairman and chief financial officer and a member of the office of the chairman.
Monaco joined HFS from American Express Co, where he was executive vice president and chief financial officer as well as a member of the planning and policy committee.
Monaco will be elected to the HFS board at the next shareholder meeting, HFS said.
Monaco, Snodgrass and Holmes will report to Henry Silverman, chairman and chief executive officer of HFS.
HFS said the new organization structure reflects the company's need to manage the continued growth of its current businesses as well as prepare for future anticipated acquisitions.
The company said it expects to complete the acquisition of Resort Condominiums International Inc, the largest provider of vacation time share exchanges, in November.
Over the past 18 months, the company has entered residential real estate and rental car industries through a series of acquisitions.
